subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should ACP `sessions_spawn` support OpenClaw skill-context injection, and which selection modes, redaction/audit fields, and child observability guarantees are part of that supported contract?
rationale: The feature decides whether trusted OpenClaw skill content may cross into external ACP harness prompts and how that interacts with native Codex skill behavior and OpenClaw session context.

options.title: Start Explicit-Only With Audit
options.body: Expose only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata.

options.title: Defer To Prompt-Contract Parity
options.body: Keep ACP skill injection blocked until #95058 settles the owning prompt layer and lifetime semantics across native and Codex harnesses.

options.title: Keep ACP Isolated
options.body: Reject core ACP skill injection and require native harness skills, MCP bridges, or plugin-specific mechanisms instead.

recommendation.title: Start Explicit-Only With Audit
recommendation.body: Expose only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP spawn/runtime feature history starts with osolmaz's ACP thread-bound agents work, making this the best available owner for the ACP contract choice.
